## Reagents and Solutions

Chemicals, drugs, biologicals, solutions and gases that are administered to subjects or used to prepare and process tissue.

### Biological material

A cell line, pluripotent stem cell line, primary-cell product, organoid line, hybridoma or tissue product, as the supplier or repository describes it. Sera, matrices and purified proteins are reagents; viral vectors are Virus constructs.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Product ID` | Text. Catalog number of the line or product as the supplier or repository writes it. |
| `Kind of material` | **Required.** Choice. What the material is, as the repository classes it. Options: Cell line, Induced pluripotent stem cell line, Embryonic stem cell line, Primary cells, Organoid line, Hybridoma, Tissue, Other. |
| `Species of origin` | Text. Species the material derives from, as the repository names it. |
| `Strain of origin` | Text. Strain or genetic background of the donor animal, as the supplier names it. |
| `Tissue of origin` | Text. Tissue the cells were taken from, as the repository names it. |
| `Cell type` | Text. Cell type the product consists of, as the supplier states it. |
| `Donor age at sampling` | Text. Age of the donor at sampling as the repository codes it, reference point included (E18, P7, 16FW, 48Y). |
| `Donor sex` | Choice. Sex of the donor as declared; mixed for pooled preparations. Options: Male, Female, Mixed, Unknown. |
| `Disease` | Text. Disease the donor carries or the line models, named with the registry's term. |
| `Reprogramming method` | Choice. How an induced pluripotent line was reprogrammed; not applicable for other kinds. Options: Sendai virus, Episomal, Lentivirus, Retrovirus, mRNA, Protein, Other, Not applicable. |
| `Genetic modification` | Text. Engineered modification the line carries, including any reporter or selection marker, as the generator states it. |
| `Growth mode` | Choice. How the line grows in culture, as the repository declares it. Options: Adherent, Suspension, Semi-adherent, 3D aggregates. |
| `Biosafety level` | Choice. Biosafety level the material requires, as the repository declares it. Options: BSL-1, BSL-2, BSL-3, Unknown. |
| `Viable cells per vial or unit (nominal)` | Integer. Viable cells per vial or unit as sold, taken from the supplier's datasheet (nominal). Range: ≥ 0. |

### Chemical reagent

A defined laboratory chemical bought as a compound, such as a salt, detergent, buffer component or solvent. Use Pharmacological agent for a drug made to act on a subject, and Histology reagent for fixatives, clearing agents and mounting media.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Product ID` | Text. Catalog or supplier product code (e.g., 'T8787', 'P6148'). |
| `Compound Name` | Text. Name of the chemical (e.g., 'Triton X-100', 'Paraformaldehyde'). |
| `Chemical Type` | **Required.** Choice. General laboratory chemicals. Tissue-processing reagents (fixatives, clearing, embedding and mounting media) belong to the Histology reagent type. Options: Detergent, Enzyme, Indicator or pH Adjuster, Salt or Buffer, Solvent, Stain or Dye, Other. |
| `Concentration / Strength` | Text. If supplied in solution (e.g., '4%', '1 M', '10X'). |
| `Molecular Weight` | Quantity with unit. Molecular weight of the chemical compound. Units: g/mol, kg/mol, Da, kDa. |
| `Purity / Grade` | Text. E.g., '≥99%', 'Analytical grade', 'ACS reagent'. |
| `Storage Conditions` | Text. E.g., 'Room temp', '4°C', 'Protect from light'. |
| `Hazard Information` | Text. Optional summary of safety hazards or GHS classification. |
| `Experimental Use Context` | Text (multi-line). Typical use cases for the reagent in experimental workflows (e.g. Perfusion, Fixation, Staining, Buffering) |

### Histology reagent

A reagent made for processing tissue after it leaves the subject, such as a fixative, permeabilization or clearing agent, or an embedding or mounting medium. Antibodies are Antibody or immunoreagent, and stains and dyes are Tracer or dye.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Product ID` | Text. Catalog number or supplier reference. |
| `Processing Role` | **Required.** Choice. Where this reagent sits in the tissue-processing chain. Options: Fixative, Cryoprotectant, Dehydration reagent, Clearing reagent, Refractive-index matching medium, Permeabilization reagent, Antigen retrieval reagent, Blocking reagent, Embedding medium, Mounting medium, Decalcification reagent, Other. |
| `Composition` | Text (multi-line). Active constituents and their concentrations as supplied. |
| `Concentration` | Text. Concentration as supplied, before any working dilution. |
| `Refractive Index` | Number. Refractive index, for clearing, index-matching, and mounting media. Range: ≥ 0. |
| `pH` | Number. pH as supplied. Range: ≥ 0 and ≤ 14. |
| `Contains Antifade` | Yes/no. Whether a mounting medium contains an antifade agent. |
| `Storage Conditions` | Text. Recommended storage conditions. |
| `Hazard Information` | Text (multi-line). Safety and handling information. Many fixatives and clearing reagents are toxic. |

### Antibody or immunoreagent

An antibody or other binding reagent bought to detect a target, such as a primary antibody, a conjugated secondary, a nanobody or a streptavidin conjugate. Dyes and tracers that label without binding a specific target are Tracer or dye.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Product ID` | Text. Supplier product code or catalog number. |
| `Target Antigen` | **Required.** Text. What the reagent binds to (e.g., 'GFAP', 'c-Fos', 'NeuN'). |
| `Reagent Type` | **Required.** Choice. General classification of the reagent. Options: Primary Antibody, Secondary Antibody, Fluorescent Label, DNA Counterstain, Other. |
| `Host Species` | Text. Host in which the antibody was raised (e.g., 'Rabbit', 'Mouse'). |
| `Reactivity Species` | Text. Species the antibody is reactive against (e.g., 'Rat', 'Mouse', 'Human'). |
| `Clonality` | Choice. Whether the antibody is monoclonal or polyclonal. Options: Monoclonal, Polyclonal, Recombinant, Unknown. |
| `Conjugated Fluorophore or Enzyme` | Text. E.g., 'Alexa Fluor 488', 'HRP', 'None'. |
| `Validated Applications` | Multi-select. Supported or validated experimental applications. Options: IHC, ICC, Western Blot, Flow Cytometry, Immunoprecipitation, Other. |
| `Recommended Dilution` | Text. Recommended dilution (e.g., '1:500', '2 µg/mL'). |
| `Storage Conditions` | Text. E.g., '4°C', '-20°C', 'Avoid repeated freeze/thaw cycles'. |

### Medical or carrier gas

A gas bought for use on subjects or in the rig, such as oxygen, medical air, carbogen, CO₂ or a premixed blend, whether as anesthetic carrier, for euthanasia or to gas a bath. Volatile anesthetics such as isoflurane are Pharmacological agents.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Product ID` | Text. Catalog number or supplier reference. |
| `Gas` | **Required.** Choice. Gas or gas mixture supplied. Options: Oxygen, Medical air, Carbogen (95% O₂ / 5% CO₂), Carbon dioxide, Nitrogen, Nitrous oxide, Argon, Helium, Other. |
| `Composition` | Text. Exact mixture, for blended or custom gases. |
| `Purity Grade` | Text. Supplier purity or regulatory grade. |
| `Supply Form` | Choice. How the gas is delivered to the rig. Options: Cylinder, House line, Concentrator, Generator, Other. |

### Pharmacological agent

A drug made to act on a subject or tissue, such as an anesthetic, analgesic, antibiotic or receptor agonist or antagonist. File by what the product is made for: a compound bought for lab chemistry is a Chemical reagent even when it is pharmacologically active.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Product ID` | Text. Catalog or supplier ID (e.g., 'C2128'). |
| `Active Ingredient` | **Required.** Text. Primary pharmacologically active substance (e.g., 'Ketamine', 'Buprenorphine', 'Isoflurane'). |
| `Concentration` | Text. Stated strength of the active ingredient (e.g., '10 mg/mL', '0.1%', '50 µg/tablet'). |
| `Dosage Form` | Choice. Physical form in which the drug is supplied. Options: Solution, Suspension, Tablet, Capsule, Injection, Topical, Patch, Other. |
| `Route of Administration` | Choice. Typical method of administration in experiments. Options: Intraperitoneal (IP), Intravenous (IV), Subcutaneous (SC), Oral, Topical, Inhalation, Intracerebral, Other. |
| `Pharmacological Category` | **Required.** Choice. Broad category of action or use. Options: Analgesic, Anesthetic, Antibiotic, Neuroactive, Recreational, Vehicle, Experimental, Other. |
| `Pharmacological Class` | Text. Mechanistic or therapeutic class (e.g., 'NSAID', 'GABA agonist', 'NMDA antagonist'). |
| `Formulation` | Text. List of excipients, solvents, or carriers (e.g., 'in 10% DMSO + saline'). |
| `Storage Conditions` | Text. E.g., '4°C', '-20°C', or 'Protect from light'. |
| `Purity / Grade` | Text. E.g., '≥98%', 'USP', 'Analytical grade'. |
| `Experimental Use Context` | Multi-select. Contexts in which this agent is typically used. Options: Surgical, Behavioral, Electrophysiology, Histology, Imaging, Other. |

### Physiological solution

A solution that living tissue or a subject is kept in or given, such as saline, PBS, Ringer's or aCSF. Use Histology reagent for solutions that fix or process tissue, and Pharmacological agent when the solution is itself a drug.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Composition` | **Required.** Text (multi-line). Full recipe or formula (e.g., '0.9% NaCl in H2O', 'aCSF with 10 mM HEPES'). |
| `Target pH value` | Number. Target pH value as numeric value (e.g., '7.4'). Range: ≥ 0. |
| `Osmolality` | Text. In mOsm/kg, if known (e.g., '300 mOsm'). |
| `Storage Conditions` | Text. E.g., 'Room temperature', '4°C', 'Frozen'. |
| `Preparation Instructions` | Text (multi-line). Steps for preparing or dissolving the solution (e.g., buffer components, filter sterilization). |
| `Sterile` | Yes/no. Is the solution sterile? |
| `Purpose / Use` | Multi-select. What is the primary use case for this solution? Options: Vehicle, Perfusion, Fixation, Dissection, Buffering, Storage, Slice Preparation, Other. |

### Tracer or dye

A dye or tracer that labels structures or reveals connections without binding a specific antigen, such as a retrograde tracer, a lipophilic dye, a histological stain or an injection marker. Labels delivered genetically by a virus are Virus constructs.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Product ID` | Text. Catalog number or supplier reference (e.g., 'D282', 'F347'). |
| `Type of Dye or Tracer` | **Required.** Choice. Function or classification of the dye/tracer. Options: Fluorescent Tracer, Lipophilic Dye, Retrograde Tracer, Anterograde Tracer, Histological Dye, Vital Stain, Injection Marker, Other. |
| `Fluorophore` | Text. Fluorophore or spectral tag used (e.g., 'Alexa Fluor 555', 'FITC'). |
| `Route of Application` | Choice. How the dye is typically applied. Options: Injection, Perfusion, Topical, Incubation, Other. |
| `Excitation Peak` | Quantity with unit. Peak wavelength for excitation (e.g., 550 nm). Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Emission Peak` | Quantity with unit. Peak wavelength for emission (e.g., 665 nm). Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Solvent / Vehicle` | Text. Solvent used for preparation (e.g., 'DMSO', 'Saline', 'Ethanol'). |
| `Storage Conditions` | Text. E.g., '4°C, dark', '-20°C'. |
| `Preparation Instructions` | Text (multi-line). Preparation or dilution steps before application. |
| `Experimental Use Context` | Multi-select. Typical applications of this tracer or dye. Options: Circuit Tracing, Histology, Injection Visualization, Vital Staining, Other. |

### Virus construct

A viral vector as designed, such as an AAV carrying a calcium indicator or an opsin under a cell-type promoter, identified by its plasmid or repository entry. The titered preparation in your freezer is Virus solution stock pointing at this entry.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Product ID` | Text. A unique identifier for the virus construct as defined by the supplier. |
| `Virus type` | Choice. The type of virus used as the vector for gene delivery. Options: Adenovirus, Lentivirus, Adeno-associated virus (AAV), Retrovirus, Herpes simplex virus (HSV), Baculovirus. |
| `Capsid` | Text. The protein shell of the virus that encloses its genetic material. Capsid modifications can affect the virus's targeting and delivery efficiency. |
| `Promoter` | Text. The DNA sequence that initiates the transcription of the inserted gene. Different promoters can control the level and location of gene expression. |
| `Gene` | Text. The gene of interest that is being delivered by the virus. This could be a therapeutic gene, a reporter gene, or any other gene used in research. |
| `Reporter` | Text. A reporter gene included in the virus construct that produces an easily observable phenotype for monitoring the expression of the gene of interest. |
| `Other element` | Text. Any additional genetic elements included in the construct such as regulatory sequences, enhancers, or other genes that assist or modify the primary gene's expression. |

## Device-Linked Consumables

Recording, stimulation and optical hardware that is implanted, mounted on a subject or attached to a rig, together with the connectors and electrode materials that link it to the acquisition system.

### Connector component

A part that joins an implant to recording or stimulation hardware, such as an electrode interface board, a connector, an adapter, a tether or a commutator. Subject-mounted assemblies such as fiber cannulas are Consumable devices.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Product ID` | Text. Catalog number or supplier reference. |
| `Class` | **Required.** Choice. Category of interconnect hardware. Options: Electrode interface board (EIB), Connector, Adapter, Cable assembly, Commutator, Pin header, Protective cap, Other. |
| `Connector Family` | Text. Manufacturer connector series, which determines what it mates with. |
| `Contact Count` | Integer. Number of electrical contacts. Range: ≥ 0. |
| `Gender` | Choice. Mating gender of the connector. Options: Male, Female, Hermaphroditic, Not applicable. |
| `Compatible With` | Text. Devices or headstages this component mates with. |
| `Mass` | Quantity with unit. Mass of the component, which matters for chronic headcap load. Units: mg, g. |

### Consumable device

A manufactured device dedicated to or used up on one subject that no more specific type covers, such as a headstage, a microdrive, a drive mount, a fiber-optic cannula assembly or a miniscope baseplate. Probes, arrays and fibers have their own design types.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Product ID` | Text. Supplier or catalog identifier (e.g., 'DORIC_MFC_2x200'). |
| `Device Class` | **Required.** Choice. Subject-mounted assemblies. Interconnect hardware (EIBs, connectors, adapters, commutators) belongs to the Connector component type. Options: Headstage, Headstage Adapter, Miniscope Baseplate, Microdrive, Drive Mount, Fiber Cannula Assembly, Thermal Interface Board, Custom Fixture, Other. |
| `Compatible Systems` | Text. E.g., 'Neuropixels', 'Inscopix', 'Open Ephys', 'Doric'. |
| `Physical Dimensions` | Text. Key geometry (e.g., '1.25 mm ferrule, 5 mm length'). |
| `Material` | Text. Main material (e.g., stainless steel, zirconia, PEEK, plastic). |
| `Connectivity` | Text. Connector/interface type (e.g., 'LC/PC', 'Omnetics', 'pin header'). |
| `Storage Conditions` | Text. E.g., 'Room temperature', 'Dry box', 'Protect from dust'. |
| `Experimental Use Context` | Multi-select. Intended or validated experimental uses. Options: Chronic Implantation, Acute Recording, Optogenetics, Imaging, Behavioral Interface, Other. |

### ECoG array design

A surface electrode array design for electrocorticography: a grid or strip of contacts on a flexible substrate that lies on the dura, the brain surface or the skull. Penetrating probes are Silicon probe designs; the arrays you hold are ECoG array stock.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Product ID` | Text. A unique identifier for the ECoG array design as defined by the supplier. |
| `Contact layout` | Choice. Arrangement family of the contacts on the array; rows, columns and pitch are recorded separately. Options: Not specified, Strip (single row or column), Grid, Other. |
| `Contact rows` | Integer. Number of contact rows in a regular grid or strip; omit for irregular layouts. Range: ≥ 1. |
| `Contact columns` | Integer. Number of contact columns in a regular grid or strip; omit for irregular layouts. Range: ≥ 1. |
| `Custom-manufactured design` | Choice. Whether the manufacturer made this as a custom design; excludes later modifications to individual arrays. Options: Not specified, Custom design, Standard design. |
| `Simultaneous recording channels` | **Required.** Integer. Maximum number of independent recording signals supported simultaneously; this can be lower than the total contact count. Range: ≥ 1. |
| `Contacts (total)` | **Required.** Integer. Total recording contacts on the array, including selectable contacts not recorded simultaneously; excludes dedicated reference contacts. Range: ≥ 1. |
| `Contact material` | Text. Exposed contact material when uniform across the array. |
| `Contact shape` | Choice. Source-specified shape shared by all recording contacts. Options: Not specified, Circular, Square, Rectangular, Other. |
| `Contact diameter` | Quantity with unit. Exposed diameter of a circular contact; give the area instead for other shapes. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Contact area` | Quantity with unit. Nominal exposed area of one contact when uniform; this does not specify contact shape. Units: nm², µm², mm², m². |
| `Pitch along a row` | Quantity with unit. Center-to-center contact spacing along a row of the array; equal to the column pitch on a square grid. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Pitch along a column` | Quantity with unit. Center-to-center contact spacing along a column of the array; omit on a single-row strip. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Substrate material` | Text. Flexible carrier material the contacts are embedded in, as the supplier names it. |
| `Array thickness` | Quantity with unit. Nominal overall thickness of the array body, as the source prints it. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Array length` | Quantity with unit. Overall extent of the array body along its rows (x); excludes tails and cables. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Array width` | Quantity with unit. Overall extent of the array body along its columns (y); excludes tails and cables. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Contact groups` | Table of rows. Groups of contacts that differ in shape, size or material, such as stimulation pads among recording contacts. |
| `Contact groups › Contact group ID` | Text. Identifier for a group of contacts sharing these specifications. |
| `Contact groups › Contact IDs` | List of integers. Numeric IDs of the contacts in this group, as used in the contact coordinates. Omit when unknown. |
| `Contact groups › Contact shape` | Choice. Shape explicitly specified for these contacts; never inferred from area alone. Options: Not specified, Circular, Square, Rectangular, Other. |
| `Contact groups › Area` | Quantity with unit. Exposed area of each contact in this group, as specified by the source. Units: nm², µm², mm², m². |
| `Contact groups › Width` | Quantity with unit. Source-specified extent of each contact in this group along a row. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Contact groups › Height` | Quantity with unit. Source-specified extent of each contact in this group along a column. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Contact groups › Contact material` | Text. Exposed contact material for the contacts in this group. |
| `Contact coordinates` | Object. Center of every recording contact as parallel lists, in the supplier's drawing frame: x along the rows, y along the columns. |
| `Contact coordinates › X coordinates` | **Required.** Multi-select. Position of each contact along the row direction, one value per contact, in the shared frame. |
| `Contact coordinates › Y coordinates` | **Required.** Multi-select. Position of each contact along the column direction, one value per contact; the cable side is recorded under Tails. |
| `Contact coordinates › Contact IDs` | **Required.** List of integers. Numeric contact IDs, one per coordinate: the source's numbering where it numbers contacts, otherwise diagram numbering. |
| `Contact coordinates › Coordinate unit` | **Required.** Choice. Length unit shared by every coordinate below. Options: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Reference contacts` | Table of rows. Dedicated reference or ground contacts on the array, one row each; they are not counted among the recording contacts. Coordinates share the contact frame. |
| `Reference contacts › Reference ID` | **Required.** Text. The source's name for this contact, for example ref or gnd. |
| `Reference contacts › Role` | Choice. Whether the source designates this contact as a reference or a ground. Options: Not specified, Reference, Ground. |
| `Reference contacts › Coordinate unit` | Choice. Length unit of the x and y position below. Options: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Reference contacts › X coordinate` | Number. Position of the contact along the row direction, in the frame shared with the contact coordinates. |
| `Reference contacts › Y coordinate` | Number. Position of the contact along the column direction, in the shared frame. |
| `Reference contacts › Contact shape` | Choice. Shape explicitly specified for this contact; never inferred from area alone. Options: Not specified, Circular, Square, Rectangular, Other. |
| `Reference contacts › Area` | Quantity with unit. Exposed area of this contact, as specified by the source. Units: nm², µm², mm², m². |
| `Reference contacts › Width` | Quantity with unit. Source-specified extent of this contact along a row. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Reference contacts › Height` | Quantity with unit. Source-specified extent of this contact along a column. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Reference contacts › Material` | Text. Exposed material of this contact when it differs from the recording contacts. |
| `Body outlines` | Table of rows. Outline of each separately drawn piece of the array body as a polygon in the contact frame, closed across the tail roots; one row per piece. |
| `Body outlines › Outline unit` | **Required.** Choice. Length unit shared by the outline x and y lists of this piece. Options: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Body outlines › Outline x` | **Required.** Multi-select. Vertex x positions of this piece's outline in drawing order. |
| `Body outlines › Outline y` | **Required.** Multi-select. Vertex y positions paired with outline x, in the frame shared with the contact coordinates. |
| `Tails` | Table of rows. Ribbons or cables leaving the array body, one row each, in the supplier's order; the first row is the rotation reference. |
| `Tails › Direction` | Choice. Which way the tail leaves the body on the supplier's drawing, as the contacts are stored. Options: Not specified, Left (as drawn), Right (as drawn), Up (as drawn), Down (as drawn), Other. |
| `Tails › Coordinate unit` | Choice. Length unit of the exit point below. Options: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Tails › Exit x` | Number. Where the tail's center line crosses the body outline, along the row direction, in the contact frame. |
| `Tails › Exit y` | Number. Where the tail's center line crosses the body outline, along the column direction. |
| `Tails › Width` | Quantity with unit. Nominal width of the tail across its run, at its widest where the source gives a maximum. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Tails › Length` | Quantity with unit. Nominal length from the body outline to the connector end, unfolded. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Openings` | Table of rows. Holes, slots and windows through the array body, one row per group of identical openings, with their centers when known. |
| `Openings › Shape` | Choice. Shape of each opening in this group. Options: Not specified, Circular, Rectangular, Slot (rounded ends), Other. |
| `Openings › Diameter` | Quantity with unit. Diameter of each circular opening in this group. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Openings › Width` | Quantity with unit. Extent of each non-circular opening along a row (x). Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Openings › Height` | Quantity with unit. Extent of each non-circular opening along a column (y). Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Openings › Coordinate unit` | Choice. Length unit shared by the center lists of this group. Options: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Openings › Center x` | Multi-select. Center of each opening along the row direction, in the contact frame; omit when positions are unknown. |
| `Openings › Center y` | Multi-select. Center of each opening along the column direction, paired with center x. |
| `Package options` | Table of rows. Published compatible connector, cable and accessory options for this design, one row each. |
| `Package options › Part number` | Text. Supplier's orderable identifier for this package, when it has one. Each row needs a part number or a name. |
| `Package options › Package name` | Text. What the package is in words, including its connector when the source states one; omit when the part number says it all. |

### Electrode component

A loose part from which an electrode is built or completed, such as a reference or ground wire, a screw electrode, a silver chloride pellet or contact foil. Use Single wire electrode for wire meant to record or stimulate on its own.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Product ID` | Text. Catalog number or supplier reference. |
| `Role` | **Required.** Choice. What this contact is supplied for. The material role recorded on a procedure remains authoritative for a given use. Options: Reference, Ground, Recording, Stimulating, Combined reference and ground, Other. |
| `Physical form` | Choice. Physical form of the contact. Options: Wire, Screw, Pellet, Foil, Mesh, Pin, Other. |
| `Conductor Material` | Choice. Conductor material, which sets the electrochemical properties of the contact. Options: Silver, Silver / silver chloride, Platinum, Platinum-iridium, Gold, Stainless steel, Tungsten, Nichrome, Carbon, Other. |
| `Insulation` | Text. Insulation material, or 'bare' if uninsulated. |
| `Diameter` | Quantity with unit. Conductor diameter. Units: µm, mm. |
| `Nominal Impedance` | Text. Manufacturer-quoted impedance, with the test frequency. |

### Optic fiber design

An optical fiber or fiber implant design used to deliver or collect light, as in optogenetics or fiber photometry. Lenses, prisms and windows are Optical components; the fibers you cut, build or buy are Optic fiber stock.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Product ID` | Text. A unique product identifier for the optic fiber design as defined by the supplier. |
| `Numerical aperture` | Number. The numerical aperture (NA) of the optic fiber. Range: ≥ 0. |
| `Wavelength minimum` | Quantity with unit. The minimum wavelength the optic fiber transmits efficiently without significant loss. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Wavelength maximum` | Quantity with unit. The maximum wavelength the optic fiber can handle. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Fiber type` | **Required.** Text. Type of fiber used in the optic fiber design, influencing how light propagates. |
| `Core diameter` | **Required.** Quantity with unit. Diameter of the fiber core affecting transmission properties like attenuation and bandwidth. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Cladding diameter` | Quantity with unit. Diameter of cladding layer around the fiber core, crucial for keeping the light signals within the core by reflection. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Coating diameter` | Quantity with unit. Diameter of the external protective coating of the optic fiber, protecting it from physical damage and environmental factors. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Core material` | Text. Material or composition of the optic fiber core impacting its refractive index and transmission characteristics. |
| `Cladding material` | Text. Material or composition of the cladding layer, having a lower refractive index than the core for reflection within the fiber. |
| `Coating material` | Text. Material or composition of the outer coating providing durability and protection. |

### Optical component

A passive optical element other than a fiber, such as a GRIN lens, cranial window glass, a coverslip, a microprism, a filter or a relay lens. Use Optic fiber design for fibers, and Consumable device when the optics come built into a mounted assembly.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Product ID` | Text. Supplier or catalog ID (e.g., 'GRIN1234', 'MP-0.5mm'). |
| `Optical Component Type` | **Required.** Choice. General class of optical element. Options: GRIN Lens, Cranial Window, Cover Glass, Microprism, Beamsplitter, Optical Filter, Relay Lens, Other. |
| `Material` | Text. E.g., glass, quartz, sapphire, polymer. |
| `Physical Dimensions` | Text. E.g., '1.0 mm diameter × 4 mm length', '3×3×1 mm prism'. |
| `Surface Coating` | Text. E.g., anti-reflective, hydrophobic, no coating. |
| `Wavelength minimum` | Quantity with unit. The minimum wavelength of light that the optic component is designed to handle. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Wavelength maximum` | Quantity with unit. The maximum wavelength of light that the optic component can handle. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Sterile` | Yes/no. Is this item provided sterile by the manufacturer? |
| `Storage Conditions` | Text. E.g., 'Room temperature', 'Dry box', 'Avoid moisture'. |
| `Experimental Use Context` | Multi-select. Contexts in which this component is typically used. Options: Chronic Imaging, Widefield Imaging, Two-Photon Imaging, Optogenetics, Histology, Other. |

### Silicon probe design

A silicon probe design for extracellular recording, such as a Neuropixels or a multishank probe, defined by its shanks and recording-site layout. Surface arrays are ECoG array designs; the probes you hold are Silicon probe stock.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Product ID` | Text. A unique identifier for the silicon probe design as defined by the supplier. |
| `Recording-site layout` | Choice. Arrangement family of the recording sites; column alignment and coordinates are recorded separately. Options: Not specified, Linear, Edge, Tetrode, Stereotrode, Poly2 (two columns), Poly3 (three columns), Poly4 (four columns), Poly5 (five columns), Buzsaki, Grid, Mixed, Other. |
| `Site column alignment` | Choice. Whether adjacent site columns sit at the same heights or are shifted against each other. Options: Not specified, Aligned rows, Shifted rows. |
| `Custom-manufactured design` | Choice. Whether the manufacturer made this as a custom design; excludes later modifications to individual probes. Options: Not specified, Custom design, Standard design. |
| `Simultaneous recording channels` | **Required.** Integer. Maximum number of independent recording signals supported simultaneously; this can be lower than the total site count. Range: ≥ 1. |
| `Recording sites (total)` | Integer. Total physical recording sites, including selectable sites not recorded simultaneously; excludes dedicated reference contacts. Range: ≥ 1. |
| `Number of shanks` | **Required.** Integer. Number of separate penetrating shanks in this probe design. Range: ≥ 1. |
| `Shank length` | Quantity with unit. Nominal tip-to-base length shared by all shanks; use individual dimensions when shanks differ. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Shank pitch` | Quantity with unit. Center-to-center distance between adjacent shanks in a uniform array. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Shank width` | Quantity with unit. Nominal width at the widest point of the shank, shared by all shanks; tapers narrow towards the tip. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Shank width at the sites` | Quantity with unit. Width of the shank alongside the recording sites; a tapered shank is narrower here than at its widest point. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Shank thickness` | Quantity with unit. Nominal thickness shared by all shanks; use individual dimensions when shanks differ. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Recording-site material` | Text. Exposed recording-site material when uniform; use site groups when materials differ. |
| `Recording-site shape` | Choice. Source-specified shape shared by all recording sites; use site groups when shapes differ. Options: Not specified, Circular, Square, Rectangular, Other. |
| `Vertical column pitch` | Quantity with unit. Center-to-center spacing along one site column; excludes offsets between shifted columns. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Horizontal site pitch` | Quantity with unit. Source-defined center-to-center site pitch across the shank. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Recording-site area` | Quantity with unit. Nominal exposed recording-site area when uniform; this does not specify site shape. Units: nm², µm², mm², m². |
| `Individual shanks` | Table of rows. Identified shanks: their sites, nominal dimensions when not uniform, and outline when known. A shank row takes precedence over the shared scalars. |
| `Individual shanks › Shank ID` | **Required.** Text. Identifier of the shank in the source drawing. |
| `Individual shanks › Site IDs` | List of integers. Numeric IDs of the recording sites on this shank, in source numbering; omit when unknown. |
| `Individual shanks › Length` | Quantity with unit. Nominal length from the shank tip to its base. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Individual shanks › Width` | Quantity with unit. Nominal width of this shank at its widest point. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Individual shanks › Thickness` | Quantity with unit. Nominal thickness of this shank. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Individual shanks › Outline unit` | Choice. Length unit shared by the outline x and y lists of this shank. Options: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Individual shanks › Outline x` | Multi-select. Polygon vertex x positions of this shank's outline, tip included, in drawing order. |
| `Individual shanks › Outline y` | Multi-select. Polygon vertex y positions paired with outline x, increasing away from the tip, in the frame shared with the site coordinates. |
| `Recording-site groups` | Table of rows. Groups of sites sharing shape, size or material; a group takes precedence over the shared site scalars. List site IDs only when the source establishes them. |
| `Recording-site groups › Site group ID` | Text. Identifier for a group of sites sharing these specifications. |
| `Recording-site groups › Site IDs` | List of integers. Numeric site IDs in source numbering (zero- or one-based); do not renumber. Omit when unknown. |
| `Recording-site groups › Site shape` | Choice. Shape explicitly specified for these sites; never inferred from area alone. Options: Not specified, Circular, Square, Rectangular, Other. |
| `Recording-site groups › Area` | Quantity with unit. Exposed area of each recording site in this group, as specified by the source. Units: nm², µm², mm², m². |
| `Recording-site groups › Width` | Quantity with unit. Source-specified horizontal extent of each recording site in this group. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Recording-site groups › Height` | Quantity with unit. Source-specified vertical extent of each recording site in this group. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Recording-site groups › Recording-site material` | Text. Exposed recording-site material for the sites in this group. |
| `Recording-site coordinates` | Object. Center of every recording site as parallel lists; any origin, shared with the shank outlines. |
| `Recording-site coordinates › X coordinates` | **Required.** Multi-select. Position of each site across the shank width, one value per site, in the shared frame. |
| `Recording-site coordinates › Y coordinates` | **Required.** Multi-select. Position of each site along the shank, increasing away from the tip, one value per site. |
| `Recording-site coordinates › Site IDs` | **Required.** List of integers. Numeric site IDs in source numbering, one per coordinate; never renumbered. |
| `Recording-site coordinates › Coordinate unit` | **Required.** Choice. Length unit shared by every coordinate below. Options: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Reference contacts` | Table of rows. Dedicated reference or ground contacts on the probe, one row each; they are not counted among the recording sites. Coordinates share the recording-site frame. |
| `Reference contacts › Reference ID` | **Required.** Text. The source's name for this contact, for example ref, gnd or tip. |
| `Reference contacts › Role` | Choice. Whether the source designates this contact as a reference or a ground. Options: Not specified, Reference, Ground. |
| `Reference contacts › Shank ID` | Text. Shank carrying this contact, matching a row of the shanks table; omit on single-shank designs. |
| `Reference contacts › Coordinate unit` | Choice. Length unit of the x and y position below. Options: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Reference contacts › X coordinate` | Number. Position of the contact across the shank width, in the frame shared with the recording-site coordinates. |
| `Reference contacts › Y coordinate` | Number. Position of the contact along the shank, increasing away from the tip, in the shared frame. |
| `Reference contacts › Shape` | Choice. Shape explicitly specified for this contact; never inferred from area alone. Options: Not specified, Circular, Square, Rectangular, Other. |
| `Reference contacts › Area` | Quantity with unit. Exposed area of this contact as specified by the source. Units: nm², µm², mm², m². |
| `Reference contacts › Width` | Quantity with unit. Source-specified horizontal extent of this contact. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Reference contacts › Height` | Quantity with unit. Source-specified vertical extent of this contact. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Reference contacts › Material` | Text. Exposed material of this contact when it differs from the recording sites. |
| `Package options` | Table of rows. Published compatible assembly, connector and accessory options for this design, one row each. |
| `Package options › Part number` | Text. Supplier's orderable identifier for this package, when it has one. Each row needs a part number or a name. |
| `Package options › Package name` | Text. What the package is in words, including its connector when the source states one; omit when the part number says it all. |

### Single wire electrode

A single insulated wire used as an electrode, such as a tungsten, stainless steel or platinum-iridium microwire, bought to record, stimulate or build tetrodes. Reference and ground parts that are not plain wire are Electrode components.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Product ID` | Text. A unique identifier for the wire electrode as defined by the supplier. |
| `Material` | Text. The type of material used for the conductive part of the electrode. Common materials include stainless steel, platinum, and gold, each providing different levels of conductivity and biocompatibility. |
| `Insulation/Coating` | Text. The type of insulation or coating used for electrical insulation. |
| `Diameter` | Quantity with unit. The diameter of the wire, which affects its flexibility, impedance, and recording surface area. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |
| `Insulation diameter` | Quantity with unit. The outer diameter of the insulation or coating. Units: nm, µm, mm, m. |

## Surgical Consumables

Materials and disposables used during surgery to fix, close or support implants, from cements and screws to sutures and blades.

### Adhesive or cement

A material that bonds or seals during surgery, such as dental acrylic, light-cured cement, cyanoacrylate glue or silicone elastomer. Use Implant or fixation material for structural parts, and Fastener or anchor for screws and pins.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Product ID` | Text. Catalog number or supplier reference. |
| `Type` | **Required.** Choice. Category of adhesive, cement, or sealant. Options: Dental cement, Acrylic polymer, Cyanoacrylate glue, Silicone elastomer, Epoxy, UV-curing adhesive, Bone wax, Tissue adhesive, Other. |
| `Number of Components` | Integer. Number of parts that must be mixed before use (1 for single-component products). Range: ≥ 1. |
| `Mixing Ratio` | Text. Manufacturer-recommended ratio for multi-component products. |
| `Curing Method` | Choice. How the product is cured after application. Options: Air cure, UV cure, Chemical cure, Thermal cure, Other. |
| `Working Time` | Text. Time available for positioning before the product sets. |
| `Storage Conditions` | Text. Recommended storage conditions. |
| `Biocompatible` | Yes/no. Whether the product is biocompatible for in vivo use. |

### Fastener or anchor

A screw, pin or anchor that holds an implant or headcap to bone, including skull screws that also serve as ground or reference. Use Adhesive or cement for what bonds them, and Implant or fixation material for the parts they hold.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Product ID` | Text. Catalog number or supplier reference. |
| `Type` | **Required.** Choice. Category of fastener or anchor. Options: Bone screw, Skull anchor, Machine screw, Nut, Washer, Pin, Clamp, Other. |
| `Thread Size` | Text. Thread designation or gauge. |
| `Length` | Quantity with unit. Overall length of the fastener. Units: mm, µm, inch. |
| `Head Type` | Text. Head or drive geometry. |
| `Material` | Choice. Material the fastener is made from. Non-magnetic and non-conductive options matter for imaging and recording. Options: Stainless steel, Titanium, Brass, Nylon, PEEK, Gold plated, Other. |
| `Conductive` | Yes/no. Whether the fastener conducts, which matters when it doubles as a reference or ground contact. |
| `Biocompatible` | Yes/no. Whether the fastener is biocompatible for in vivo use. |

### Implant or fixation material

Structural hardware or material an implant is built from or fixed with, such as a headpost, a recording chamber, a baseplate or shielding mesh. Bonding materials are Adhesive or cement; manufactured assemblies are Consumable devices.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Product ID` | Text. Catalog number or supplier reference. |
| `Type` | **Required.** Choice. Structural implant hardware. Adhesives and cements belong to the Adhesive or cement type; screws and anchors to Fastener or anchor. Options: Headpost, Chamber, Baseplate, Shielding mesh, Other. |
| `Preparation Instructions` | Text (multi-line). Preparation steps before application. |
| `Storage Conditions` | Text. Recommended storage conditions. |
| `Biocompatible` | Yes/no. Whether the material is biocompatible for in vivo use. |

### Surgical disposable

A single-use item consumed during surgery or handling, such as a suture, a needle, a blade, a swab, a drape or gloves. Anything that becomes part of an implant is Implant or fixation material.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Product ID` | Text. Catalog number or supplier reference. |
| `Type` | **Required.** Choice. Category of surgical disposable. Options: Scalpel blade, Needle, Syringe, Suture, Gauze/Swab, Surgical drape, Catheter, Other. |
| `Material` | Text. Primary material (e.g., stainless steel, plastic, absorbable). |
| `Specification` | Text. Short free-text detail to disambiguate similar items (size, gauge, blade number, etc.). |
| `Sterile` | Yes/no. Whether the item is sterile. |

## Other types

### External Identifiers

Add external identifiers from databases like NCBI, JAX, DOI, etc. Include URLs when available.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Source` | **Required.** Choice. Options: NCBI, JAX, DOI, UniProt, PubMed, Addgene, Sigma-Aldrich, Thermo Fisher, Abcam, Cell Signaling, Custom, Other. |
| `Identifier` | **Required.** Text. |
| `URL (optional)` | Text. |
